scope: Claude root intake of the Codex J1-R3 handoff, a timer finding, the RC6 package and the J1-R4 local preparation (inputs, command plan, root gates and a reviewed live-window runner). Local only; nothing ran on Linux, systemd or PostgreSQL and no host contact occurred.
finding: The staging fallback unit is started by its timer every five minutes and is a protected unit. Its ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic is compared strictly by the controller (before launch versus prove) and by the root postflight gate, so a J1 window of several minutes would very likely fail for a benign product reason. J1-R3 was therefore not proposed for execution.
ownerDecision: 2026-10-11: fix the timer rule first, then test, audit and a new GO.
rule: Only astra-pine-market-fallback-stage.service may differ, only in ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic, only by a strict increase, only when it is loaded, inactive, dead, MainPID 0 and has no Job on both sides with NRestarts unchanged. Every other unit and field stays strict. An empty allowlist behaves exactly like RC5.

rc6.receipt: schema v2: equal stays strict raw equality; equivalent, timerActivatedUnitsSha256 and at most one allowance (unit hash, field, deltaUs) were added; the receipt carries no unit names
rc6.unchanged: harness v8.2, measurement tool v3, product revision eb532ffd and the other 12 adapters

j1r4.step0BootCheck: read-only boot id hash check before any write
j1r4.limitsUnchanged: 11 cases, 285 s + 30 s, 512 MiB, CPU 100%, TasksMax 32 / 26, disk B 1 GiB with 20 / 40 MiB/s IO limits, harness-only socket guard, product tool hashes before and after
j1r4.runner: admit, run-row and accept-run: the operations worker runs only one root-admitted row at a time; no retries; any stderr stops; records are write-once

checks.controllerMutation: 157 killed; 9 not killed, all pre-RC6 gaps (5 never planted, 4 survived)

audits: Six Opus audits (RC6 twice, ops preparation twice, runner twice). No open high or medium finding; the remaining low items are runbook wording, folded into the runbook.
disclosures: A timer start during a health probe or the controller snapshot, or the unit running at that moment, still fails or refuses the attempt.
A manual start of the fallback unit inside the window cannot be told apart from a timer start.
A reboot after the boot check gives BOOT_DRIFT at prestart and consumes the attempt.
The two-warning check is not atomic with the internal start preflight.
Any refusal, drift or unknown consumes the attempt; there is no retry.
Disk B is not a hard quota and the socket guard is not kernel isolation.
notRun: RC6 on Linux, systemd or PostgreSQL
the real Windows OpenSSH path of the runner
incidents: During local testing one tester ran a command that ended all local node processes once; later briefs forbid process kills.
nextAction: Owner GO for one J1-R4 attempt; then root dispatches one Claude operations worker under the runbook.
